sentences.en: I've been looking at ocean biodiversity, that's the diversity of species that live in the world's oceans.
sentences.zh: I一直在研究海洋生物多样性，也就是生活在世界海洋中的物种的多样性。

sentences.en: About 20 years ago biologists developed the idea of what they called 'biodiversity hotspots'.
sentences.zh: 大约20年前，生物学家提出了所谓‘生物多样性热点地区’的概念。

sentences.en: These are the areas which have the greatest mixture of species, so one example is Madagascar.
sentences.zh: 这些地区拥有最丰富的物种混合度，例如马达加斯加就是一个例子。

sentences.en: These hotspots are significant because they allow us to locate key areas for. 031 focusing efforts at conservation.
sentences.zh: 这些热点地区意义重大，因为它们能帮助我们确定开展保护工作的关键区域。

sentences.en: Biologists can identify hotspots on land, fairly easily, but until recently, very little was known about species distribution and diversity in the oceans, and no one even knew if hotspots existed there.
sentences.zh: 生物学家可以相对容易地在陆地上识别出热点地区，但直到最近，人们对海洋中物种的分布与多样性知之甚少，甚至没人知道海洋中是否存在此类热点。

sentences.en: Then a Canadian biologist called Boris Worm did some research in 2005 on data on ocean species that he got from the fishing industry.
sentences.zh: 随后，一位名叫鲍里斯·沃姆（Boris Worm）的加拿大生物学家于2005年利用渔业部门提供的海洋物种数据展开了一项研究。

sentences.en: Worm located five hotspots for large ocean predators like sharks, and looked at what they had in common.
sentences.zh: 沃姆定位出五个大型海洋掠食者（如鲨鱼）的热点地区，并分析了它们的共同特征。

sentences.en: The main thing he'd expected to find was that they had very high concentrations of food, but to his surprise that was only true for four of the hotspots - the remaining hotspot was quite badly off in that regard.
sentences.zh: 他原本主要预期会发现这些地区拥有极高的食物浓度，但令他惊讶的是，这一情况仅适用于其中四个热点地区——剩下的那个热点地区在这方面却明显匮乏。

sentences.en: But what he did find was that in all cases, the water at the surface of the ocean had relatively high temperatures, even when it was cool at greater depths, so this seemed to be a factor in supporting a diverse range of these large predators.
sentences.zh: 但他确实发现，在所有情况下，海洋表层水温均相对较高，即使深层海水温度较低，因此这似乎是支撑这类大型掠食者多样性的关键因素。

sentences.en: However, this wasn't enough on its own, because he also found that the water needed to have enough oxygen in it - so these two factors seemed necessary to support the high metabolic rate of these large fish.
sentences.zh: 然而，单靠这一点还不够，因为他还发现水中必须含有足够的氧气——因此，这两个因素似乎都是支撑这些大型鱼类高代谢率所必需的。

sentences.en: A couple of years later, in 2007, a researcher called Lisa Ballance, who was working in California, also started looking for ocean hotspots, but not for fish - what she was interested in was marine mammals, things like seals.
sentences.zh: 几年后，即2007年，一位在加州工作的研究人员丽莎·巴拉恩斯（Lisa Ballance）也开始寻找海洋热点地区，但她关注的并非鱼类，而是海洋哺乳动物，例如海豹等。

sentences.en: And she found three places in the oceans which were hotspots, and what these had n common was that these hotspots were all located at boundaries between ocean currents, and this seems to be the sort of place that has lots of the plankton that some of these species feed on.
sentences.zh: 她发现了海洋中三处热点地区，而这些地区的共同点在于：它们均位于洋流交汇的边界地带，而这类地点似乎富含某些物种赖以生存的浮游生物。

sentences.en: So now people who want to protect the species that are endangered need to get as much information as possible.
sentences.zh: 因此，如今那些希望保护濒危物种的人士需要尽可能多地获取相关信息。

sentences.en: For example, there's an international project called the Census of Marine Life.
sentences.zh: 例如，有一个名为‘海洋生物普查’（Census of Marine Life）的国际项目。

sentences.en: They've been surveying oceans all over the world, including the Arctic.
sentences.zh: 他们已对全球各地的海洋（包括北冰洋）展开了调查。

sentences.en: One thing they found there which stunned other researchers was that there were large numbers of species which live below the ice - sometimes under a layer up to 20 metres thick.
sentences.zh: 他们在北冰洋的一项发现令其他研究人员震惊：大量物种栖息于海冰之下——有时冰层厚度甚至达20米。

sentences.en: Some of these species had never been seen before.
sentences.zh: 其中一些物种此前从未被人类观测到过。

sentences.en: They've even found species of octopus living in these conditions.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至在这些条件下发现了章鱼的物种。

sentences.en: And other scientists working on the same project, but researching very different habitats on the ocean floor, have found large numbers of species congregating around volcanoes, attracted to them by the warmth and nutrients there.
sentences.zh: 而参与同一项目的其他科学家，研究的是海底截然不同的栖息地，他们发现大量物种聚集在火山周围，被那里的温暖和养分所吸引。

sentences.en: However, biologists still don't know how serious the threat to their survival is for is each individual species.
sentences.zh: 然而，生物学家目前仍不清楚每一种物种所面临的生存威胁究竟有多严重。

sentences.en: So a body called the Global Marine Species Assessment is now creating a list of endangered species on land, so they consider things like the size of the population how many members of one species there are in a particular place - and then they look at their distribution in geographical terms, although this is quite difficult when you're looking at fish, because they're so mobile, and then thirdly they calculate the rate at which the decline of 037 the species is happening.
sentences.zh: 因此，一个名为‘全球海洋物种评估’的机构目前正在建立一份陆地濒危物种名录，他们考察的因素包括种群规模（即某一特定地区内某物种的个体数量），然后从地理分布角度进行分析——不过，对鱼类而言，这相当困难，因为它们活动性极强；第三步是计算该物种数量下降的速度。

sentences.en: So far only 1,500 species have been assessed, but they want to increase this figure to 20,000.
sentences.zh: 迄今为止，仅有1500个物种接受了评估，但他们希望将这一数字提升至20,000。

sentences.en: For each one they assess, they use the data they collect on that species to produce a map showing its distribution.
sentences.zh: 对于每一个接受评估的物种，他们都利用所收集的数据绘制一张显示其分布范围的地图。

sentences.en: Ultimately they will be able to use these to figure out not only where most species are located but also where they are most threatened.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们将能够借助这些地图，不仅确定大多数物种的集中分布区域，还能识别出它们面临最大威胁的区域。

sentences.en: So finally, what can be done to retain the diversity of species in the world's oceans?
sentences.zh: 那么，最后的问题是：我们能做些什么来维持世界海洋中物种的多样性？

sentences.en: Firstly, we need to set up more reserves in our oceans, places where marine species are protected.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们需要在海洋中设立更多保护区，即对海洋物种实施保护的区域。

sentences.en: We have some, but not enough.
sentences.zh: 我们目前已有一些保护区，但数量尚不足够。

sentences.en: In addition, to preserve species such as leatherback turtles, Audioscripts which live out in the high seas but have their nesting sites on the American coast, we need to create corridors for migration, so they can get from one area to another safely.
sentences.zh: 此外，为保护棱皮龟等物种——它们生活在公海，却在美国海岸筑巢——我们需要建立迁徙走廊，使其能安全地从一个区域抵达另一个区域。

sentences.en: As well as this, action needs to be taken to lower the levels of fishing quotas to prevent overfishing of endangered species.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还需采取行动降低捕捞配额，以防止对濒危物种的过度捕捞。

sentences.en: And finally, there's the problem of 'by-catch'.
sentences.zh: 最后，还有‘兼捕’问题。

sentences.en: This refers to the catching of unwanted fish by fishing boats - they're returned to the sea, but they're often dead or dying.
sentences.zh: 这指的是渔船意外捕获非目标鱼类——这些鱼会被放归大海，但往往已死亡或濒临死亡。

sentences.en: If these commercial fishing boats used equipment which was more selective, so that.
sentences.zh: 如果这些商业渔船采用更具选择性的捕捞设备，

sentences.en: only the fish wanted for consumption were caught, this problem could be overcome.
sentences.zh: 只捕获供人类食用的鱼类，这一问题便可得到解决。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So does anyone have any
sentences.zh: 那么，大家有什么问题吗？
